newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds sees asset sales of $900 mln.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds sees asset sales of $900 mln.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co expects its ongoing portfolio review to result in proceeds of about $900 million, chief executive Jeremiah Sheehan said.
He told analysts Wednesday the company will use the proceeds to reduce debt, adding this will reduce annual interst expenses $70 to $75 million.
Sheehan said this "would improve our debt/equity ratio to 30/70, compared to 43/57 at the end of 1996."
Over the next two years, he continued, "we are committed to a reduced capital spending program of $250 to $300 million per year, excluding acquisitions."
"This compares to our previous two-year average of about $440 million," Sheehan said, explaining "Our exit from a number of capital intensive businesses will help us accomplish this."
However, he does expect the reduced spending to include expansion of the 56 percent owned Worsley alumina plant in Australia to just under three million metric tonnes a year from 1.7 million.
Sheehan said "I could seek board approval (of Worsley) as soon as August." The other 44 percent is held by Gencor Industries Inc's Billiton.

He said the internal reorganization triggered by the performance review the company first discussed with analysts in October 1996 "has resulted in personnel reductions in various operational and staff functions at our corporate headquarters" in Richmond, Va.
"The number of positions involved is approximarly 600 and most affected employees have been notified," Sheehan said.
This is expected to reduce corporate overhead costs by $40 million annually, he noted.
He said Reynolds has "not yet reached a decision about our Can and Packaging businesses" and is considering various sale and spinoff options for all or a portion of these businesses.
"The reason these businesses remain under study is that we have been identified a number of interesting opportunities, and each must be carefully considered."
Sheehan said "keeping all of these businesses is not an option we are considering. We plan to optimize their value one way or another."

He reiterated most of the actions resulting from the portfolio review should be completed by the end of this year and these actions will begin to contribute to earnings this year and will have an even greater impact in 1998.
"We expect to enter 1998 a dramatically improved company, repositioned for growth, against a backdrop of strong industry fundamentals," he concluded.
"That's possible" was Sheehan's response to questions about the $0.90 per pound average price analysts are forecasting for aluminum in 1998.
He projected a increase in demand for the metal "above three percent this year" and of five percent in 1998.
He told the analysts Reynolds sees "several excellent investment opportunities currently available to us.
In addition to Worsley, these include "additional investment in our wheel business and several projects in our Flexible Packaging business.
"While we have no current plans to invest in any major greenfield expansions of our smelting business, there will be opportunities for high-return cost reduction projects in our plants.
"In addition to these internal opportunities, we will be looking for high-return acquisition projects in several of our businesses," Sheehan said.
"One focus will be to participate in the ongoing consolidation of the metals distribution industry through acquisitions by our RASCO unit.
"Additionally, we will look for opportunities to grow the Flexible Packaging business through U.S. and foreign acquisitions."
((-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610))
